title: One-Pot Tomato & White Bean Orzo
description: Tender orzo, white beans, and tomatoes cook together into a cozy pantry dinner with very little cleanup.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use small pasta and add a little extra broth as needed.
Skip Parmesan for a dairy-free meal.

steps.text: Combine the orzo, tomatoes, beans, broth, and seasonings.
Simmer until the orzo is tender, then finish with Parmesan if using.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large saucepan or deep skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup orzo and stir for 1 minute.

Stir in 1 can diced tomatoes, 1 drained can white beans, 2 cups broth, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 15–18 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is tender. Add a splash of broth or water if it gets too thick.
Stir in 1/4 cup Parmesan if using and serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Add a splash of water or broth when reheating.

title: Ham, Cabbage & Egg Fried Rice
description: Leftover rice, diced ham, cabbage, and fluffy egg turn into a quick skillet dinner with familiar ingredients.
substitutions: Leave out the ham for egg-and-cabbage fried rice.
Use frozen peas or diced carrots in place of some cabbage.
Serve with a squeeze of lime if available.

steps.text: Cook the eggs and remove them from the skillet.
Cook the cabbage and ham, then fry the rice.
Return the fluffy eggs and season.

cookSteps.text: Heat half of the 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Beat 2 eggs, add them to the skillet, and gently scramble just until set. Transfer the eggs to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, 2 cups sliced cabbage, and 1 cup diced ham. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until the cabbage softens and the ham is hot.
Add 3 cups cold leftover rice. Cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking up clumps and stirring until the rice is hot and lightly toasted. Stir in 2 tablespoons soy sauce and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Break the cooked eggs into fluffy pieces, fold them back into the rice, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Tuna & White Bean Toast
description: Tuna and white beans make a creamy, filling pantry topping for crisp toast in about ten minutes.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use plain Greek yogurt instead of mayonnaise.
Add chopped celery, cabbage, or pickle if you have it.

steps.text: Mash the tuna and bean mixture.
Toast the bread and pile the mixture on top.

cookSteps.text: In a bowl, lightly mash 1/2 can white beans. Stir in 1 drained can tuna, 2 tablespoons mayonnaise, 1 teaspoon mustard, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Toast 4 slices bread until crisp, about 3–5 minutes depending on your toaster.
Divide the tuna-bean mixture over the toast and serve.

storage: Refrigerate leftover tuna-bean mixture up to 2 days. Toast bread fresh when serving.

title: Small-Batch Caramel Banana Oat Crisp
description: Two ripe bananas bake under a brown-sugar oat topping for a warm, inexpensive dessert sized for a small household.
substitutions: Use quick oats if that is what you have.
Use half banana and half sliced apple.
Add a spoonful of caramel sauce at serving time if available.

steps.text: Layer the bananas with brown sugar.
Mix and scatter the oat topping.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Arrange 2 sliced ripe bananas in a small baking dish and sprinkle with 1 tablespoon brown sugar.
In a bowl, mix 1/2 cup oats, 1/4 cup flour, 1/4 cup brown sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon. Work in 3 tablespoons softened butter until crumbly, then scatter over the bananas.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the edges bubble and the oat topping is golden.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat gently or eat chilled.
